sources.citation: The slim 24 V 5 A (120 W) DIN-rail switch-mode supply, a common control-panel class. Typical published figures, paraphrased (not one vendor's): 24 V DC output, 5 A continuous; load regulation within about ±1 % from no load to full load. The output resistance is the worst-case slope of that band (0.24 V over 5 A, 48 mΩ): the band is a tolerance, and real units typically droop less; body about 40 mm wide, 125 mm tall and 114 mm deep from the rail.

Overload protection of the class: a current limit that typically engages between about 105 % and 150 % of the rated current, recovering automatically (hiccup mode) once the fault is removed. 120 % (6 A) is taken, inside that band. Paraphrased from manufacturers' datasheets for the class.

game-design: 100 ms in current limit before the output shuts down, then 1 s off before each restart attempt, a hiccup period of 1.1 s. Datasheets for the class describe hiccup recovery but rarely give its timing; these are chosen to look like it (a short burst, then about a second off).
game-design: the V− and V+ output screw terminals sit on the front face near the top, 16 mm apart; not modelled on a product.

The output screw terminals of the 24 V 5 A DIN-rail supply class, from several makers' public datasheets, paraphrased (not one vendor's): copper conductors of about 24 to 12 AWG (some 26 to 14 or 20 to 10), solid, stranded or stranded in a ferrule, a tightening torque of about 0.4 to 0.6 N·m (0.5 N·m is taken) and a strip length of about 7 to 10 mm (8 ± 1 mm is taken). Copper only (not rated for aluminium).
game-design: one conductor per terminal is the rating; two fit physically and make a worse termination (D8). Not a published figure.
game-design: conductors enter the output terminals from the top face (125 mm) above each screw and leave along +y; not modelled on a product.
The class clips onto a 35 mm DIN rail (IEC 60715) and takes its body width, about 40 mm (the din-psu-120w-class source), along the rail.

game-design: unverified. DIN-rail power supplies commonly have slotted and Pozidriv combination terminal screws (common practice for IEC-style terminals, not read from one datasheet); the drive type is a name and its size is not modelled.

game-design: the supply's output terminals take the branch-circuit screw class's contact resistance, 0.3 mΩ at the marked torque with copper at 20 °C (NBS Building Science Series 103, 1977, measured 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ on good branch-circuit screw terminals; ADR 0018 §4.1). BSS 103 measured wiring-device terminals, not a power supply's box clamps, so applying it here is a game-design choice.

game-design (ADR 0018 §3.3), for F3.6's hot-spot node: the heat path takes the screw class's calibrated 0.026 W/K (no better figure for a supply's terminal); the clamp's heat capacity, 0.5 J/K, is a physics estimate for a smaller box clamp, about 1.3 g of brass and steel × about 380 J/(kg·K).

game-design: the supply's screw terminals are box clamps (a rising cage that closes around the conductor), so bare strands are held (ADR 0018 §4.3); the cage grips 7 mm of conductor, inside the 8 ± 1 mm strip. Not modelled on a product.
